optimization_strategy.bottleneck: Two hidden ATen layout copies dominate the non-conv time: an implicit NCHW→NHWC transpose of x inside conv1 plus two per-call weight channels_last conversions. They are 7.6% of steady GPU time (2,125 us / 36 launches = 3 per forward) and do zero math.
optimization_strategy.optimisation method: Replace all three TensorIterator layout copies with shared-memory tiled transpose kernels: a 32x33-tile NCHW→NHWC activation transform (mirror of the existing norm_silu_res_t epilogue) and a per-output-channel weight (O,I,3,3)→(O,3,3,I) transform, so both read and write streams are fully coalesced.

optimization_strategy.evidence: nsys steady-state table: `at::native::elementwise_kernel` = 7.6% of per-forward GPU time (2,125 us over 36 launches = exactly 3 per forward), matching the three layout copies in forward (2 explicit `_cl_weight` calls + 1 implicit NCHW→NHWC of `res` performed by ATen because conv1 sees a NCHW input with a channels_last weight). These kernels do no math, so they are pure removable overhead; the small shape (2x256x64x64) only reaches 1.0106x because the two shape-independent weight copies are a fixed tax on a 0.363 ms forward. That a tiled transpose is the right shape here is shown by our existing `norm_silu_res_t_kernel`, whose 32x33-tile transpose hits gpu__dram_throughput.avg.pct_of_peak = 89.52% with the SOL rule stating it is 'utilizing greater than 80.0% of the available compute or memory performance' — near roofline, whereas a TensorIterator transpose copy pays sector amplification on its strided side. Ruled out (a) gn_partial_kernel: despite dram 61.41% and a 47.98% UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule hit, it is only 2.4% of steady time (663 us), capping any gain below 1%; (b) the allowed method CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers: only ~15 launches per forward against ~2.4 ms of GPU work, so launch overhead is already hidden, and replay would add a full static-buffer copy of the 67 MB input (~75 us) — a net regression. I therefore deviate from allowed_methods; the mechanism is coalescing/transaction-size, targeting the largest non-vendor time block.
optimization_strategy.expected_metric_change: New layout kernels should reach gpu__dram_throughput.avg.pct_of_peak ≈ 85-90% (like norm_silu_res_t's 89.52%) versus the strided ATen copy; the `elementwise_kernel` row drops from 7.6% of steady time toward ~0 and is replaced by transforms costing ~2x tensor bytes; l1tex sector/excessive-sector counts for the layout step ↓; end-to-end time ↓ ~4-6% on the mid/large shapes and ~10%+ on the small/awkward shapes (fixed weight-copy tax removed). Anti-regression: shared memory is 32*33*4 = 4,224 B/block and 9,216 B for the weight kernel, keeping ≥12 blocks/SM (no drop below the current 86.57% warps_active of norm_silu_res_t); total DRAM traffic must stay exactly one read + one write of each transformed tensor (no extra staging buffer); numerics unchanged (pure data movement, float32); the tail guards must write every element for P%32!=0 and C%32!=0 (verify 1x256x131x131).
